coverage_notes.note: The Permitted Exception referenced in Section 3.3(e), the Order Form, OpenAI Policies, Third-Party Service Terms, and other incorporated documents are not supplied in full; their content cannot be inferred.

Sections 4.1–4.3 establish ownership, assignment, and responsibilities or limits on OpenAI’s use; they do not state a general license to exploit Input or Output. Section 4.4’s similarity statement creates no operative behavioral duty.

P0001 includes party and defined-term context plus a representation concerning authority to enter the Agreement; the authority representation is not an activity constraint and is not modeled as a license rule.

The Security Measures, Audit Reports, DPA, Healthcare Addendum, Service Credit Terms, Order Form, Pricing Page, and OpenAI Policies are incorporated or referenced but not supplied here; their substantive terms are not inferred.

Several operative provisions cannot be faithfully represented with the supplied activity/object schema: OpenAI’s security-measure and audit-report delivery duties; the incorporated DPA obligations; the PHI-specific prohibition; payment, tax, invoice-dispute, and billing-information duties; suspension and account-control provisions; and the requirement that a Recipient be responsible for certain personnel breaches. Related target paragraphs are marked UNRESOLVED where applicable.
Section 9.1’s reservation that Customer receives no ownership rights in the Services is noted in scope, but the schema does not provide an ownership-rights activity.

Section 11.3 also requires OpenAI to delete Customer Content within 30 days after termination, subject to legal-retention and written-agreement exceptions, and permits retention of Abusive Customer Content and certain sharing related to it. These deletion, retention, and sharing provisions cannot be faithfully expressed with the available activities; accrued-payment and minimum-commitment consequences are likewise outside the activity vocabulary.

Section 13 includes indemnification obligations, mitigation duties, and claim-handling procedures that cannot be faithfully represented as the available activities. Section 13.3 also requires Customer to comply promptly with reasonable instructions, including instructions to replace, modify, or cease use of a Service; the general instruction-following duty and replacement/modification paths are not fully representable here.
Section 13.1 incorporates Service-Specific Terms Indemnity as of the Effective Date, but that external text is not supplied and is not inferred.
Section 12.1–12.2 and Sections 12.3(b)–(e) contain warranties, disclaimers, and descriptions of Beta Service characteristics or risks, which are not activity constraints for this extraction.
Section 14 limits liability and specifies exceptions; it does not grant, prohibit, or require an activity.

Section 15 contains operative dispute-resolution procedures and restrictions that cannot be faithfully represented with the supplied activities and objects: mandatory arbitration; informal-resolution steps and a 60-day period; settlement conferences; tolling of limitations; arbitration initiation, forum, procedure, and fee allocation; exceptions for small-claims and equitable-relief claims; individual-proceeding and class-action restrictions; batch arbitration; and severability rules.

Section 15.2 requires Customer to complete the Informal Dispute Resolution Form and OpenAI to notify Customer at the Account email address. Both Parties must attend an individual settlement conference if either requests one during the informal-resolution period. The referenced form is not supplied.

Section 15.3 incorporates the arbitration provider’s rules for administrative and arbitrator costs; those rules are not supplied. Section 15.7 provides batching when 25 or more claimants represented by the same or similar counsel file demands raising substantially similar disputes within 90 days; the agreement defines a Batch as up to 50 claimants. The stated fewer-than-50 exception and the remaining batching terms are preserved in the source but cannot be represented as license activity rules. No missing external text has been inferred.

The supplied text does not define Supported Countries and Territories, Restricted Party List, or the applicable external trade-control details, and does not provide the incorporated Order Forms, Service-Specific Terms, OpenAI Policies, DPA, or Section 8 suspension terms. Their content is not inferred.

Section 16.7 imposes operative restrictions and conditions on assignment of the Agreement, including OpenAI’s Affiliate assignment permission and a 30-day prior written notice condition for either Party’s assignment to a successor to substantially all assets or business. Assignment of the Agreement is not faithfully expressible using the supplied activity and object categories.

Section 16.5 imposes operative notice-method, recipient, address, copy, and deemed-receipt rules. Sending contractual notices is not faithfully expressible using the supplied activity and object categories.

Section 16.13(a) also imposes update-notice duties on OpenAI. Those duties, and the full mechanics for OpenAI’s update action, are not represented as licensee activities; the customer’s continued-use acceptance mechanism is modeled separately.

Sections 16.1–16.4, 16.6, and 16.8–16.10 principally state agreement interpretation, severability, waiver, relationship, liability, or beneficiary terms rather than activity constraints in the supplied schema. Section 16.14 states the rights basis for Government Entity customers without creating a distinct additional activity permission in the supplied text.

This target contains definitions only. They identify terms and their meanings but do not, by themselves, impose operative permissions, prohibitions, or duties. The definition of “Permitted Exception” does not establish an operative exception absent the provision that uses it.
The DPA, Pricing Page, Order Forms, and other referenced materials are not included here; no terms from them are inferred.

P0019 contains definitions only. It does not itself impose operative duties or grant permissions. The referenced external Security Measures, Service Credit Terms, Service-Specific Terms, Sharing and Publication Policy, Usage Policies, and supported-country lists are not included; no rules have been inferred from them.

rules.source_excerpt: This OpenAI Services Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered as of the Effective Date between the organization agreeing to these terms (“Customer”) and the OpenAI Contracting Party defined below (“OpenAI”). In this Agreement, OpenAI and Customer are each referred to as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.” Capitalized terms not defined in the Agreement have the meanings provided in the Order Form. Customer represents it is lawfully able to enter into this Agreement and, if it is entering into the Agreement for an entity, that it has legal authority to bind that entity. By clicking “I agree,” accepting the Order Form, or using the Services, Customer agrees to this Agreement.
rules.scope_note: Agreement preamble; use of Services is one of the stated methods by which Customer agrees to the Agreement.
rules.condition_explanation: acceptance_by_click_order_form_acceptance_or_service_use means Customer accepts by clicking “I agree,” accepting the Order Form, or using the Services.

rules.source_excerpt: 1.1. Services Term. OpenAI will deliver the Services to Customer for the Services Term. The Services Term will be listed on the Order Form. Unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing, increases in the Services purchased during a Services Term will have a prorated term ending concurrently with the then‑current Services Term.
rules.scope_note: Section 1.1; OpenAI must deliver the Services to Customer for the Services Term listed on the Order Form.
rules.condition_explanation: Services Term is specified in the applicable Order Form; increases purchased during a Services Term are prorated to end with the then-current Services Term unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

obligation_items.content: Deliver the Services to Customer for the Services Term.
obligation_items.trigger: During the Services Term listed on the Order Form, subject to any written agreement otherwise for the term of service increases.

rules.source_excerpt: 1.2. Renewal. Renewal Terms, if any, and whether the Services auto renew, will be listed on the applicable Order Form. Notice of non‑renewal or scope reduction must be given at least thirty days before the start of the next Renewal Term. If Customer reduces its license count, quantity, or minimum commitment, OpenAI may adjust or remove discounts offered to Customer based on its prior purchase.
rules.scope_note: Section 1.2; applies when Customer gives notice of non-renewal or scope reduction for a Renewal Term.
rules.condition_explanation: notice_at_least_30_days_before_next_renewal_term means the notice is given at least 30 days before the next Renewal Term starts. Whether renewal occurs and whether Services auto-renew are determined by the Order Form.

obligation_items.content: Give notice of non-renewal or scope reduction at least 30 days before the start of the next Renewal Term.
obligation_items.trigger: When Customer elects non-renewal or scope reduction for a Renewal Term.

rules.source_excerpt: b. Purchases. The Services may be configured to allow Authorized Purchasers to purchase additional licenses, quantities, or volumes of Services. Customer is responsible for understanding the Services settings that allow additional purchases. OpenAI will charge Customer for additional licenses, quantities, or volumes of Services for the remainder of the then‑current Services Term based on Customer’s then‑current price unless otherwise set forth on the Order Form.
rules.scope_note: Section 1.3(b); Authorized Purchasers may purchase additional licenses, quantities, or volumes only where the Services are configured to allow those purchases.
rules.condition_explanation: services_configured_to_allow_additional_purchases is the stated configuration condition. The charge is based on Customer’s then-current price for the remainder of the then-current Services Term unless the Order Form provides otherwise.

obligation_items.content: Pay the charge for additional licenses, quantities, or volumes for the remainder of the then-current Services Term at the then-current price, unless the Order Form provides otherwise.
obligation_items.object: Additional Services purchased by Authorized Purchasers
obligation_items.trigger: When an Authorized Purchaser purchases additional licenses, quantities, or volumes through a configuration that permits such purchases.

rules.source_excerpt: a. Usage. OpenAI provisions the Services to specific entities using dedicated workspaces and organizational IDs. Customer Affiliates may use the Services under Customer’s Account, which means Customer and its Affiliates usage will occur in the same workspace and under the same organizational ID. Customer will be responsible and liable for all acts and omissions of its Affiliates that access the Services in connection with this Agreement.
rules.scope_note: Section 1.4(a); Affiliate use under Customer’s Account occurs in the same workspace and organizational ID as Customer. Customer is responsible and liable for Affiliate acts and omissions connected with the Agreement.
rules.condition_explanation: affiliate_accesses_services_in_connection_with_agreement means the Affiliate accesses the Services in connection with this Agreement.

obligation_items.content: Be responsible and liable for all acts and omissions of its Affiliates that access the Services in connection with the Agreement.
obligation_items.object: Affiliate use of Services under Customer’s Account
obligation_items.trigger: When a Customer Affiliate accesses the Services in connection with this Agreement.

rules.source_excerpt: b. Separate Purchases. If Customer Affiliates’ purchase and use of the Services is intended to be separate from Customer’s, then the Affiliate must execute a separate Order Form. OpenAI will then create a separate workspace and organizational ID for that Affiliate and provision the Services accordingly. If Customer Affiliates enter into Order Forms under this Agreement they will be bound by this Agreement.
rules.scope_note: Section 1.4(b); when Affiliate purchase and use is intended to be separate from Customer’s, the Affiliate must execute a separate Order Form; OpenAI then creates a separate workspace and organizational ID and provisions Services accordingly. Affiliates entering Order Forms under the Agreement are bound by it.
rules.condition_explanation: affiliate_purchase_and_use_intended_separate_from_customer is the stated condition for requiring a separate Order Form.

obligation_items.content: Execute a separate Order Form for separate Affiliate purchase and use.
obligation_items.trigger: When Affiliate purchase and use of the Services is intended to be separate from Customer’s.

obligation_items.content: Create a separate workspace and organizational ID and provision the Services accordingly.
obligation_items.object: Separate Affiliate Services account and workspace
obligation_items.trigger: After the Affiliate executes the separate Order Form.

rules.source_excerpt: 1.5. Usage‑based Services. If Customer purchases Services based on usage, Customer acknowledges that OpenAI will charge Customer the Fees for the Services based on the usage calculated by OpenAI.
rules.scope_note: Section 1.5; applies to Services purchased based on usage.
rules.condition_explanation: customer_purchases_usage_based_services means Customer purchases Services on a usage basis; fees are based on usage calculated by OpenAI.

obligation_items.content: Pay Fees for usage-based Services based on usage calculated by OpenAI.
obligation_items.trigger: When Customer purchases Services based on usage.

rules.source_excerpt:
2.1. General. The Agreement governs Customer’s access to and use of the Services. Customer may access and use the Services in accordance with the Agreement.
2.2. Use. OpenAI grants Customer a non‑exclusive right to access and use the Services during the Term. This includes the right to use OpenAI’s API to integrate the Services into Customer Applications and to make Customer Applications available to End Users.
rules.scope_note: Sections 2.1–2.2; non-exclusive right to access and use Services during the Term, including use of the API to integrate Services into Customer Applications and make those applications available to End Users.
rules.condition_explanation: during_term means while the Agreement’s Term is in effect. in_accordance_with_agreement requires compliance with applicable Agreement terms.

rules.source_excerpt: 2.2. Use. OpenAI grants Customer a non‑exclusive right to access and use the Services during the Term. This includes the right to use OpenAI’s API to integrate the Services into Customer Applications and to make Customer Applications available to End Users.
rules.scope_note: Section 2.2; includes using OpenAI’s API to integrate Services into Customer Applications and making those applications available to End Users.
rules.condition_explanation: during_term means while the Agreement’s Term is in effect; the integration and availability remain subject to the Agreement.

rules.source_excerpt: 2.3. Modifications. OpenAI may update the Services periodically. If an OpenAI update materially reduces the Services functionality, OpenAI will notify Customer at the Account email address. Within five business days of receipt of this notice, Customer may choose to terminate the Agreement by providing thirty days written notice. This termination right will not apply to updates made to features provided on a beta or evaluation basis.
rules.scope_note: Section 2.3; termination right for an OpenAI update materially reducing Services functionality; excluded for features provided on a beta or evaluation basis.
rules.condition_explanation: The condition requires a material reduction in Services functionality, notice at the Account email address, Customer’s election within five business days after receiving notice, and 30 days’ written termination notice. The right does not apply to updates to beta or evaluation features.

obligation_items.content: Give OpenAI 30 days’ written notice of termination after electing to terminate within five business days of receiving the update notice.
obligation_items.trigger: An OpenAI update materially reduces Services functionality, OpenAI notifies Customer at the Account email address, and the update is not to a beta or evaluation feature.

rules.source_excerpt: 3.1. Customer Account. Customer must provide accurate and current Account information. Customer will not share Account access credentials or individual login credentials between multiple users. Customer may not resell or lease access to its Account or any End User Account. Customer will promptly notify OpenAI if it becomes aware of unauthorized access to the Account or the Services.
rules.scope_note: Section 3.1; governs Customer Account information and access credentials, resale or lease of Account or End User Account access, and notice of unauthorized access.
rules.condition_explanation: The rule requires accurate, current Account information; prohibits sharing Account access credentials or individual login credentials between multiple users and reselling or leasing access to the Account or an End User Account; and requires prompt notice upon awareness of unauthorized access.

obligation_items.content: Provide accurate and current Account information.
obligation_items.trigger: While maintaining or using the Customer Account.

obligation_items.content: Do not share Account access credentials or individual login credentials between multiple users.
obligation_items.object: Account access credentials and individual login credentials
obligation_items.trigger: At all times.

obligation_items.content: Do not resell or lease access to the Account or any End User Account.
obligation_items.object: Account or End User Account access
obligation_items.trigger: At all times.

obligation_items.content: Promptly notify OpenAI of unauthorized access to the Account or Services.
obligation_items.trigger: Promptly after Customer becomes aware of unauthorized access.

rules.source_excerpt: 3.2. End Users. End User Accounts may only be provisioned to, registered for, and used by, a single End User. Customer is responsible for all activities that occur under its Account, including the activities of End Users with an End User Account or who access the Services through a Customer Application. Customer will obtain and maintain from End Users any consents necessary to allow Administrators to engage in the activities described in the Agreement and to allow OpenAI to deliver the Services.
rules.scope_note: Section 3.2; applies to End User Accounts, activities under Customer’s Account, and consents necessary for Administrators’ Agreement-described activities and OpenAI’s service delivery.
rules.condition_explanation: single_end_user_per_account means each End User Account is provisioned to, registered for, and used by one End User only. Necessary consents must be obtained and maintained from End Users.

obligation_items.content: Provision, register, and permit use of each End User Account for a single End User only.
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever an End User Account is provisioned, registered, or used.

obligation_items.content: Be responsible for all activities under its Account, including activities of End Users with End User Accounts or accessing Services through a Customer Application.
obligation_items.trigger: When activities occur under Customer’s Account.

obligation_items.content: Obtain and maintain from End Users necessary consents for Administrators to engage in Agreement-described activities and for OpenAI to deliver the Services.
obligation_items.trigger: Before and while the relevant Administrator activities or OpenAI service delivery occur.

rules.source_excerpt: 3.3. Restrictions. Customer will not, and will not permit End Users to: (a) use the Services or Customer Content in a way that violates applicable laws or OpenAI Policies; (b) use the Services or Customer Content in a way that violates third parties’ rights; (c) allow minors to use OpenAI Services without consent from their parent or guardian; (d) Reverse Engineer any aspect of the Services or the systems used to provide the Services; (e) except for a Permitted Exception, use Output to develop artificial intelligence models that compete with OpenAI’s products and services; (f) extract data from the Services other than as permitted through the Services; (g) buy, sell, or transfer API keys from, to, or with a third party; (h) interfere with or disrupt the Services, including circumvent any rate limits or restrictions or bypass any protective measures or safety mitigations for the Services; (i) violate or circumvent Usage Limits or otherwise configure the Services to avoid Usage Limits.
rules.scope_note: Section 3.3; applies to Customer and End Users and prohibits the listed conduct. The restriction on developing competing AI models from Output has a Permitted Exception; the definition and scope of that exception are not included in the supplied text.
rules.condition_explanation: Each atom denotes the corresponding prohibited conduct in Section 3.3(a)–(i). use_output_to_develop_competing_ai_model_without_permitted_exception applies only absent a Permitted Exception. Reverse Engineer is defined in the supplied definition context and includes specified reverse-engineering and model-extraction conduct, except where the restriction is contrary to applicable law.

obligation_items.content: Do not use the Services or Customer Content in a way that violates applicable laws or OpenAI Policies.
obligation_items.trigger: At all times.

obligation_items.content: Do not use the Services or Customer Content in a way that violates third-party rights.
obligation_items.trigger: At all times.

obligation_items.content: Do not allow minors to use OpenAI Services without consent from their parent or guardian.
obligation_items.trigger: When a minor uses OpenAI Services, unless the minor’s parent or guardian has consented.

obligation_items.content: Do not Reverse Engineer any aspect of the Services or the systems used to provide them.
obligation_items.object: Services and systems used to provide Services
obligation_items.trigger: At all times, except to the extent the restriction is contrary to applicable law.

obligation_items.content: Do not use Output to develop artificial intelligence models that compete with OpenAI’s products and services, except for a Permitted Exception.
obligation_items.trigger: When using Output to develop an AI model that competes with OpenAI’s products or services, unless a Permitted Exception applies.

obligation_items.content: Do not extract data from the Services other than as permitted through the Services.
obligation_items.trigger: When extracting data, unless extraction is permitted through the Services.

obligation_items.content: Do not buy, sell, or transfer API keys from, to, or with a third party.
obligation_items.trigger: At all times.

obligation_items.content: Do not interfere with or disrupt the Services, including by circumventing rate limits or restrictions or bypassing protective measures or safety mitigations.
obligation_items.object: Services and their limits, protective measures, and safety mitigations
obligation_items.trigger: At all times.

obligation_items.content: Do not violate or circumvent Usage Limits or configure the Services to avoid Usage Limits.
obligation_items.trigger: At all times.

rules.source_excerpt: 3.4. Third‑Party Services. Third‑Party Services may be available through the Services, which Customer may elect to use in its sole discretion. By accessing a Third‑Party Service, Customer agrees to the applicable Third‑Party Service Terms. Customer’s access or use of Third‑Party Services are governed by this Agreement and the relevant Third‑Party Service Terms.
rules.scope_note: Section 3.4; Third-Party Services may be available through the Services and Customer may elect to use them in its sole discretion. Access or use is governed by the Agreement and relevant Third-Party Service Terms.
rules.condition_explanation: customer_elects_to_access_third_party_service means Customer chooses to access or use a Third-Party Service; applicable Third-Party Service Terms are additional terms for that service.

obligation_items.content: Comply with the applicable Third-Party Service Terms when accessing a Third-Party Service.
obligation_items.trigger: Upon accessing or using a Third-Party Service.

rules.source_excerpt: 4.1. Generally. Customer and Customer’s End Users may provide Input and receive Output. As between Customer and OpenAI, to the extent permitted by applicable law, Customer: (a) retains all ownership rights in Input; and (b) owns all Output. OpenAI hereby assigns to Customer all OpenAI’s right, title, and interest, if any, in and to Output.
rules.scope_note: Section 4.1; as between Customer and OpenAI, Customer retains ownership rights in Input and owns Output; OpenAI assigns to Customer any OpenAI right, title, and interest in Output. Input and Output are distinct materials.
rules.condition_explanation: to_extent_permitted_by_applicable_law qualifies the stated allocation. The clause states ownership and assignment, not an independent license to use or distribute Input or Output.

rules.source_excerpt: 4.2. OpenAI Obligations. OpenAI will only use Customer Content as necessary to provide Customer with the Services, comply with applicable law, enforce the OpenAI Policies, and prevent abuse. OpenAI will not use Customer Content to develop or improve the Services, unless Customer explicitly agrees to such use.
rules.scope_note: Section 4.2; applies to OpenAI’s use of Customer Content. Development or improvement use is excluded unless Customer explicitly agrees.
rules.condition_explanation: The first four alternatives are stated necessary purposes. The separate development or improvement purpose is permitted only if Customer explicitly agrees. Customer Content comprises Input and Output as defined elsewhere in the Agreement.

obligation_items.content: Do not use Customer Content except as necessary to provide Customer with Services, comply with applicable law, enforce OpenAI Policies, or prevent abuse; do not use it to develop or improve Services unless Customer explicitly agrees.
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever OpenAI uses Customer Content.

rules.source_excerpt: 4.3. Customer Obligations. Customer is responsible for all Input and represents and warrants that it has all rights, licenses, and permissions required to provide Input to the Services. Customer is solely responsible for all use of the Outputs and for evaluating the accuracy and appropriateness of Output for Customer’s use case.
rules.scope_note: Section 4.3; Customer is responsible for Input, must have rights, licenses, and permissions to provide it, and is solely responsible for use and evaluation of Outputs.
rules.condition_explanation: The clause expressly imposes an Input rights representation and warranty and assigns responsibility for Output use and evaluation. It does not itself grant a right to use Output.

obligation_items.content: Have all rights, licenses, and permissions required to provide Input to the Services.
obligation_items.trigger: When providing Input to the Services.

obligation_items.content: Be solely responsible for all use of Outputs and for evaluating their accuracy and appropriateness for Customer’s use case.
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever Customer uses Output or selects Output for a use case.

rules.source_excerpt:
7.1. Use and Nondisclosure. Recipient agrees it will: (a) only use Discloser's Confidential Information to exercise its rights and fulfill its obligations under this Agreement; (b) take reasonable measures to protect the Confidential Information; and (c) not disclose the Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted in this Agreement.
7.2. Exceptions. The obligations in Section 7.1 do not apply to information that: (a) is or becomes generally available to the public through no fault of Recipient; (b) was in Recipient’s possession or known by it prior to receipt from Discloser; (c) was rightfully disclosed to Recipient without restriction by a third party; or (d) was independently developed without use of Discloser’s Confidential Information.
7.3. Permitted Disclosure. Recipient may disclose Confidential Information only to its Affiliates, employees, contractors, and agents who have a need to know and who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as restrictive as those in this Agreement. Recipient will be responsible for any breach of this Section 7 by its employees, contractors, and agents. Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, if Recipient uses reasonable efforts to notify Discloser, to the extent permitted, prior to doing so.
rules.scope_note: Section 7.1(a): applies to a Recipient’s use of the Discloser’s Confidential Information; Confidential Information includes Customer Content. Section 7.2 exceptions apply where the information is public through no fault of Recipient, was previously possessed or known, was rightfully disclosed without restriction by a third party, or was independently developed without use of the Confidential Information.
rules.condition_explanation: use_only_to_exercise_agreement_rights_or_fulfill_agreement_obligations means the Recipient uses the Discloser’s Confidential Information only for those purposes, subject to the Section 7.2 exceptions.

rules.source_excerpt:
9.1. Reservation of Rights. Except as expressly set forth herein, the Agreement does not grant: (a) OpenAI any IP Rights in Customer Content; or (b) Customer any IP Rights in the Services. Customer obtains only a limited right to use the Services, and no ownership rights are transferred to Customer or its End Users under this Agreement.

rules.source_excerpt: 11.3. Effects of Termination. If this Agreement terminates: (a) the rights granted by OpenAI to Customer will cease immediately; and (b) OpenAI will delete all Customer Content from its systems within thirty days, unless: (i) OpenAI is legally required to retain it; or (ii) Customer has agreed otherwise in writing. In addition, except for a termination by Customer for cause, if this Agreement terminates any unpaid minimum commitment amounts set forth on the Order form will become immediately due. a. Generally. OpenAI may update this Agreement, or OpenAI Policies, by providing Customer with reasonable notice, including by posting the update on OpenAI’s website. If OpenAI determines in its sole judgment that an update materially impacts Customer’s rights or obligations, OpenAI will provide Customer at least thirty days’ notice before the update is effective, unless the update is necessary for OpenAI to comply with applicable law, in which case OpenAI will provide Customer with as much notice as reasonably possible. Any other updates will be effective on the date OpenAI posts the updated Agreement or OpenAI Policy. Customer’s continued use of, or access to, the Services after an update is effective constitutes acceptance of the update. If Customer does not agree with an update, Customer may stop using the Services or terminate this Agreement under Section 11.
b. Exceptions. Except for an update to comply with applicable law, updates to this Agreement or the OpenAI Policies will not apply to: (i) Disputes between Customer and OpenAI arising prior to the update; or (ii) Order Forms signed by Customer and OpenAI (as opposed to an automated ordering page) prior to OpenAI notifying Customer of the update. rules.scope_note: Section 16.13 provides that Customer’s continued use of or access to the Services after an update becomes effective constitutes acceptance of that update. Customer may instead stop using the Services or terminate under Section 11. Update exceptions and timing are set out in Section 16.13(b).

gap_ledger.reason: Lines 86–93 govern arbitration and informal dispute resolution, including procedural duties, cost allocation, exceptions, class and batch proceedings, and severability. These actions do not fit any allowed activity; mapping them to Use or another license activity would be inaccurate.

The local PHI prohibition and its Healthcare Addendum and service-design limits are modeled. Section 5.1’s security compliance duty and conditional termination option, Section 5.2’s duty to provide Audit Reports on written request no more than once yearly, and Section 5.3’s DPA compliance rule cannot all be represented by the permitted activities. The Security Measures and DPA are absent external references and are not inferred.

Customer payment, billing-information, tax, withholding-uplift, invoice-dispute, and overdue-amount terms are captured as conditions or ancillary duties on relevant Service use without misusing Charge. OpenAI’s separate fee-charging, pricing-correction, and Services suspension or termination powers, and external Service Credit Terms, are noted as not represented or excluded in coverage_notes.

The local Customer duty to promptly suspend or terminate an End User account on OpenAI’s qualifying request is recorded. OpenAI’s direct account suspension or termination power, Services limitation or suspension powers, and associated notice, tailoring, cooperation, and restoration duties do not fit the fixed activity vocabulary.

The immutable anchors cover Sections 9.2–9.3: OpenAI’s limited necessary use of Customer Content, including extension to subcontractors and subprocessors, and the Feedback use permission. Section 9.1 reserves IP Rights except as expressly granted and states Customer obtains only a limited right to use Services with no ownership transfer; this is reservation/ownership language, not an additional activity permission or independently expressible use constraint, so no new clause is appropriate.

The immediate end of Customer's service-use rights and OpenAI's local permissions concerning abusive content are modeled. OpenAI's deletion duty and exceptions and the accrued-payment and minimum-commitment consequences have no faithful representation in the fixed activity vocabulary; the unmatched actions are deletion/retention handling and payment consequences.

Customer's duty to promptly comply with a reasonable instruction to cease Service use is modeled. The indemnity, defense, claim procedure, continued-use acquisition, replacement/modification, and other mitigation duties do not fit the fixed activity vocabulary; the unmatched actions are indemnifying/defending, claims administration, obtaining rights, and replacing or modifying Services.

The local trade-control, input, geographic-access, and continued-use rules are covered by the cited immutable anchors. Remaining operative rules in this target include contractual assignment restrictions and notice requirements (Sections 16.5 and 16.7), and OpenAI’s duty to notify Customer of updates (Section 16.13(a)); these are agreement-assignment or notice actions that do not faithfully fit any supplied activity. No additional activity clause can represent them.
